# AssemblyScript

[AssemblyScript](https://www.assemblyscript.org) looks like TypeScript and compiles straight to WebAssembly, so it's the closest you can get to writing a module in the language your page code is in. Its modules are tiny: the summary example is 10 KB, its first call compiles in about 13 ms, and later calls load it from the cache in half a millisecond.

It looks like TypeScript, but it isn't: types are WebAssembly's (`i32`, `f64`, `u8`), there's no `any` and no union types, and npm packages written for JavaScript don't work in it. Only packages written for AssemblyScript do.

## Set up

AssemblyScript builds for the browser by default. [`@assemblyscript/wasi-shim`](https://github.com/AssemblyScript/wasi-shim) makes it build a WASI program instead, with `process.argv`, `process.stdin`, `process.stdout` and `process.exit`:

```bash
npm install --save-dev --save-exact assemblyscript @assemblyscript/wasi-shim
```

`asconfig.json` extends the shim's settings and sets the release build:

```json
{
  "extends": "./node_modules/@assemblyscript/wasi-shim/asconfig.json",
  "targets": {
    "release": {
      "outFile": "summary.pb.wasm",
      "optimizeLevel": 3,
      "shrinkLevel": 2,
      "noAssert": true,
      "runtime": "stub"
    }
  }
}
```

- **The shim is required.** Without it, a module imports `env.abort` from the browser's world, and it's refused when it loads.
- **`"runtime": "stub"`** leaves out the garbage collector: a call reads, computes and exits, so nothing needs collecting, and the module is smaller. A module that builds large data in a loop can use `"incremental"` instead.

## The module

[`example/summary/assemblyscript`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/summary/assemblyscript/assembly/index.ts) counts the words of a text and returns the first twelve. AssemblyScript's standard library has no JSON, so, like the [C](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/c) example, it takes the text as it is (your code can pass a string) and prints JSON:

```ts
// what `summary --describe` prints: AssemblyScript can't embed a file, so the manifest is a string here
const manifest = `{ "description": "Summarizes a text: its first words, and a word count", ... }`

function fail(code: string, message: string): void {
  process.stderr.write(`{"code":"${code}","message":"${message}"}`)
  process.exit(1)
}

const fn = process.argv.length > 1 ? process.argv[1] : ""
if (fn == "--describe") {
  process.stdout.write(manifest)
} else if (fn != "run") {
  fail("no_such_function", "only run")
} else {
  const text = readStdin() // process.stdin.read() into a growing buffer, then String.UTF8.decode
  // ... split into words, keep the first 12
  process.stdout.write(`{"text":${jsonString(short)},"words":${words.length}}`)
}
```

To take JSON in, add a JSON package written for AssemblyScript, such as [json-as](https://github.com/JairusSW/json-as).

## Build

```bash
npx asc assembly/index.ts --target release
cp summary.pb.wasm pb_hooks/
```

The manifest says `"language": "AssemblyScript"`, since the module doesn't say it itself.

## Call it

An API route that saves a post with its summary and word count:

```ts
// pb_pages/posts.ts
export async function post(ctx: any) {
  const { body } = ctx.req.body()
  const out = await $wasm.run.async<{ text: string; words: number }>("summary", String(body ?? "")) // a string goes in as it is
  const record = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId("posts"))
  record.load({ body, summary: out.text, words: out.words })
  ctx.app.save(record)
  return ctx.res.json(201, { id: record.id, summary: out.text, words: out.words })
}
```
